full_judgment:
2. Sonali Bank Limited obtained a decree from this Court for an amount of US $ 12,7089.70 against the judgment debtors. After obtaining the said decree the plaintiff bank put the decree into execution and in that execution proceeding this Court passed an order on 10.9.86 for attachment of the shares of the judgment debtor No. 2 Khondker Mahtabuddin Ahmed which are lying with the UCBL and that is why the UCBL after coming to know about the order of attachment from the notice published in the Bangladesh Observer dated 12th April, 1987 filed the present application for vacating the order of attachment and sale in respect of the share certificates of the judgment debtor No. 2. 

 8. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, on the other hand, submits that in fact the judgment debtor No.2 is still the owner of the aforesaid share certificates. He simply deposited the same to the bank with a blank deed duly signed by him to transfer the same to others for satisfying his debts. So, for all practical purpose the judgment debtor No.2 is the owner of the impugned share certificates and as such the Sonali Bank is entitled to attach the same. It is difficult to accept the contention of Asrarul Hossain in view of the fact that the share certificates in question arc not immovable properties, rather the same are movable properties and also the same is considered as goods under the Sale of Goods Act. The judgment debtor No. 2 had delivered those Movable goods namely, share certificates to the UCBL with an authority to sell it in order to adjust its loan in part. On such delivery of goods the judgment debtor No. 2 has lost his domain, control and possession over the share Certificates. As soon as the judgment debtor had delivered such movable goods to the petitioner-bank with an authority to sell out the same in order to adjust the loan, which he had taken earlier, he ceases to have any domain, control and possession of the same. Not only that, on such delivery of possession of such movable goods the judgment debtor ceases to have exercised any right of ownership over such movable property. In such a situation it is difficult to accept the contention of Mr. Asrarul Hossain that still the judgment debtor No. 2 has got ownership over the aforesaid share certificates. The properties of a judgment debtor, either movable or immovable, can be attached in order to satisfy a decree only if the sante is in his possession and control. In the present case the petitioner UCBL is not a judgment debtor and the possession and control of the aforesaid share certificates are with the petitioner bank and as such the Sonali Bank is not entitled to attach the same in execution of the above decree,
